analysis:
Both changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/...). No production code, key handling, attestation, authorization, cache or coordinator wire code changes in the supplied units. No threat-model control (T-041 cache, TB-002 WebSocket, TB-011 authorization) is weakened by these tests.

GLM5NextPromptPolicyTests.swift (head lines 509-941): new tests cover reasoning/clear_thinking precedence, raw-schema restoration, forged internal marker rejection (x-darkbloom-original-boolean-schema fails only when actual model_type is glm5_next; caller-supplied model_type is not authority, lines 603-619), strict tool-call history correlation (exact IDs, object-only args, duplicate keys and oversized integers rejected, lines 559-576), OpenRouter reasoning-content return shapes and captured tool requests, and exact large-integer handling (lines 899-908). These tests pin fail-closed validation behavior; they do not alter it. The fixtures include SHA-256 pins of captured request bodies (lines 843-846).

GLM5NextMediaRoutingTests.swift: adds CryptoKit import, a stub tokenizer, a PreparedCapture helper, and a readiness test routing real OpenRouter clips through ingest and the processor. The helper openRouterVideo reads fixtures via #filePath-relative path and verifies SHA-256 (lines ~123-130 in head). The path is test-only, hash-checked, and reads no secrets. The test verifies that videos reach the engine instead of being refused as invalid_media; the underlying production behavior (media ingest bounds, budget reservations) is not changed in this PR as supplied.

Remaining question: the production changes that these tests exercise (thinking-object parsing, empty-args rendering, VFR video ingest, strict-tool acceptance) are not in the supplied units. Their security impact (input validation bounds, media decode budgets, DoS) should be reviewed with the production diff if it exists in another batch.
